subtitle: Capcom · Nintendo 3DS

body: Monster Hunter 4 Ultimate is Capcom's expanded Nintendo 3DS hunting adventure, released in Japan as Monster Hunter 4G. A travelling caravan takes the hunter between settlements and dangerous regions, where assignments involve tracking and defeating large creatures. Their materials become weapons and armour for later expeditions. The journey gives each encounter a purpose beyond its immediate reward: a particular creature may hold the part needed to finish a set of equipment. Choosing the next hunt therefore begins with considering what the hunter wants to make.

Ledges and climbable surfaces give attacks a new vertical dimension. Leaping from higher ground can begin an attempt to mount a monster, turning its movement into another opportunity for the group. The Insect Glaive adds mobility and a companion that gathers extracts, while the Charge Blade changes between weapon forms. Every weapon has its own commitments and recovery times. Learning when a creature is about to turn, charge or pause gives the hunter time to choose an attack that can finish before the next danger arrives.

Four hunters can cooperate locally or online, sharing the work of containing a creature and surviving its attacks. Equipment, restorative items and an understanding of the terrain all contribute to that preparation. Ultimate adds G-rank challenges and more content to Monster Hunter 4, extending the ladder of increasingly demanding hunts. The Western edition arrived in 2015. Progress remains expressed through knowledge and equipment: a familiar monster becomes more manageable when the player recognises its behaviour and brings tools suited to the task.
